setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I was talking to Kim. I think you spoke with him a couple of days ago.' Prospect: 'Yeah, yesterday.' The prospect refers back to Kim twice more — 'what I told Kim' and 'like one of the biggest goals... what I told Kim'.

prospect.name: Anthony Sosa
prospect.location: Boulder, Colorado, USA (grew up in Texas)
prospect.occupation: Mental health counsellor running his own therapy practice; sets his own schedule and recently invested in opening another arm of the business
prospect.training_background: Lifelong athlete — basketball, football, some soccer. Seven years of calisthenics and yoga with no weights, including a dedicated handstand practice. Yoga teacher with his own practice. Three to four years at an Ido Portal-lineage movement school in Boulder. Returned to weightlifting two to three years ago and gained 20 lb in a year. Just finished a 12-week strength-and-cardio programme. Serious Zouk (Brazilian partner) dancer, travels for dance events. Does 14ers in Colorado. Carb cycles, always high protein. Weighed 150-155 lb through the calisthenics years, now 175. Has tried one of Trevor's kettlebell workouts from video with a 20 lb bell.
prospect.medical: No conditions, injuries or diagnoses disclosed. Names ankles and feet as his long-standing weak area from playing sports. Says he no longer does handstand push-ups or shoulder presses at 175 lb because he will not put the extra strain on his wrists. Reports sleep being cut short on dance-event weekends.

signals: Already fit and highly trained across yoga, calisthenics, movement practice and weightlifting; explicitly framing this as going to a level he has not reached — 'can I take it to a level that I have not taken it to?'

Uses the language of the archetype unprompted: 'especially if I want to go to a next level of like my own health and like optimizing or, you know, or whatever those words we want to use, optimizing, maximizing'
Runs his own business and bought without argument over the number itself

Divergence worth noting: price was not a quality signal for him, it was a liquidity problem. Revenue of $5-6k a month, $1-2k monthly surplus, a declined Payva application and a $2,000 ceiling on what he could put down today. Profile is the_optimizer; cash position is not.

goals.text: Achieve a level of leanness and visible abdominal definition he has never managed in any training style
Learn kettlebells as a genuinely new skill and reach mastery and self-sufficiency in it — 'that fourth stage in the four stages'
Train more efficiently so there is time left for dance, business and everything else he loves
Receive coaching, support and accountability for once instead of always being the one supporting others
Prove the discipline to himself — he identified the leanness goal as being about proving he can do it
Show up more focused and present for his therapy clients by keeping his own body healthy
Keep doing 14ers and stay conditioned for altitude living in Colorado

pains.text: Has never been able to get lean despite gaining muscle easily — 'bulking was easy. Cutting was like, you know, dialing it in, so it was something that I was never able to fully dial in'
The 20 lb he gained returning to weights closed off calisthenic skills he used to have — no longer does handstand push-ups or shoulder presses because of wrist strain
Effort alone has stopped producing progress; the last 12-week programme delivered but did not move the goal that matters to him
Chronically self-directed — 'I'm so used to being able to get a program and then organize it myself' — and has never received real coaching
Previous paid personal training was worse than useless — 'I was like, man, I know more than this guy'
Ankles and feet are a persistent weak area from years of sport
Cash is tight after a recent business investment; income $5-6k/month with $1-2k left on a good month
As a therapist he is always the one giving support and never receiving it

objections.raw_quote: That would be best just because I just made, like to be honest, I just made another investment in my business, you know, to open up another part of my business, so I mean, ideally, like, for right now, like, I could put some of it in my credit card, and then another part of it, I can like, if I could do some form of payment, that would be the best.
objections.rep_response: Ran the money play properly for once. Offered the plan in the scripted framing ('Most of the guys just put it on a credit card up front, but like, do you feel like you need a payment plan?'), got permission to talk openly about finances, then worked the financial picture — monthly surplus, savings and investments, credit cards and available limit. Quoted a $1,200/month structure with interest, tried Payva third-party financing (declined), relayed a manager's suggestion of a 50/50 split, and finally landed on three payments of $2,000. He never ran the isolation question first.

objections.raw_quote: a part of me has little doubts like but can I get that same stimulus of anabolic stimulus from just kettlebells from like the, you know, the squats, you know, part of me is like, I was like, I'll just trust, you know, you don't know, you got to find out.
objections.rep_response: Answered 'Yeah, but it's different' and immediately pivoted into his own hip-dysplasia recovery story. The hypertrophy question was never actually addressed; the prospect had already talked himself past it.

tiers.label: Month-to-month structure quoted live at $1,200/month — 'that will be $1,200 because we done that. That will be a little more interest on that.' Not taken.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three payments of $2,000 — $2,000 taken on the call, then $2,000 next month and $2,000 the month after. Total $6,000 with no interest applied. Arrived at only after a $1,200/month interest-bearing plan was discussed, a Payva third-party financing application was declined, and a manager-suggested 50/50 split ($3,000 today) was tested and rejected because the prospect's card would only carry $2,000. No dates, no autopay and no written schedule were established on the call for the remaining $4,000.

prospect_financials.detail: Revenue about $5-6k/month from the therapy practice. After multiple rents including an office, 'on a good month, like one to two K a month left', which normally goes into investments or back into the business. Investments over $100k that he can access when needed, plus an untouchable 401k. One business credit card; the bank has been 'weird' about a limit increase. Payva financing application was declined on the call, which he attributed to recent large credit payments.

evidence: Payment confirmed live: 'Let's see, it just said invoice paid, $2,000.' Rep: 'Yep. Actually, I see it.'
Agreed the full structure verbally: 'So that would be the plan, is just going 2K per month? Yeah, yeah, yeah. Yeah, let's do that. That's going to work.'
Onboarding call with Trevor booked for 11:45am the next day, invite confirmed received.

Counter-evidence, and it is material: no agreement exists. The rep discovered live that the agreement email had not been sent and said 'this is totally custom-built. You don't have the agreement right now. I'll need to craft it myself, and I will send it later on today.' The client has paid $2,000 against a $6,000 commitment with nothing signed.
Counter-evidence: only $2,000 of $6,000 is collected and the remaining two instalments have no dates, no autopay and no written terms — they rest entirely on a verbal 'let's do that'.

Counter-evidence on price integrity: the same rep reported this deal to his manager an hour and a half later as a mistake — 'I closed him on 3Pay of 2K... I just totally forgot' — because instalment plans are supposed to carry interest.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor at 11:45am the following day. Rep to hand-craft and send the agreement later the same day and notify via WhatsApp. Prospect to complete the agreement and the onboarding form before the Trevor call. Primal University Skool invitation referenced as part of the second email.

notable.note: This is the deal Andrew self-reported to Chris Klevan as an error ninety minutes later in the 1-1 (data/internal_calls/2026-07-07_andrew-musial_chris-klevan.json): 'I closed him on 3Pay of 2K... there is supposed to be typically a bit of interest on that.' The management response was to honour the terms and use the concession to ask this client for a referral, timed immediately so the favour would still feel current. Three separate prices were live on this call — $6,000 upfront, $7,200 as $1,200/month with interest, and $6,000 as three interest-free instalments — and the one the client got was the cheapest, chosen by accident. Separately, this is the best-run discovery in the batch: the setter's notes were genuinely read back, past attempts were worked properly, and the reflect-back ('the game now is precision and dialing in those small pieces... You operate as an athlete right now') is the single best moment in the twelve files. The consequence frame was still skipped entirely — and Chris coached exactly this prospect type ('the cost of staying good') on the team meeting three hours after this call ended.

quality.notes: Persistent swapping. Whole rep questions sit inside the prospect's blocks, e.g. at 00:01:15 'Okay, what specifically, and what are you doing currently in terms of fitness' is attributed to the prospect, and at 00:39:57 the prospect's question 'But if I was able to put the first two grand on a credit card?' carries the rep's label. The 00:19:00 pillar presentation runs as one long unpunctuated block. Roles read from content throughout. Two long dead-air gaps in the recording — 00:39:57 to 00:42:18 and 00:44:00 to 00:46:41 — correspond to the prospect checking his credit and the Payva application, not to truncation; the call ends naturally at 00:59:48.
